package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects all Volusion-hosted stores with injected code)
package_info.why_malicious: The injected JavaScript code is designed to steal payment card details from end customers by exfiltrating sensitive data entered on checkout/payment forms to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This is a classic Magecart-style web skimmer attack, targeting thousands of online stores and their customers.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into the HTML/JavaScript of Volusion-hosted e-commerce sites (typically in a script tag or external JS file)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into the payment form submission event, collects credit card data from input fields, and exfiltrates this data to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain via a network request, resulting in theft of payment card details.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting sensitive payment data in the browser and sending it to an external, non-payment-related domain is a hallmark of web skimming attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce JavaScript should never exfiltrate payment data to third-party domains; payment data should only be sent to trusted payment processors.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Form validation scripts may read payment fields, but should not transmit data externally except to payment gateways.
key_indicators: Event listener on payment form submission
Network request to untrusted or hardcoded domain
Use of obfuscation or encoding (e.g., btoa)

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to Volusion's infrastructure and injects malicious JavaScript into customer storefronts.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is loaded by end customers visiting affected stores.

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript executes in the context of the checkout/payment page, hooking into form submission.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collection of payment card data from unsuspecting customers.

attack_chain.action: Collected payment card data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment card details for further fraud or sale.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code hooking into payment or checkout form submission events
Collection of credit card or payment data fields in client-side scripts
Outbound network requests to domains not associated with the legitimate payment processor
file_indicators: Unexpected or recently modified script tags in e-commerce site HTML
External JavaScript files loaded from untrusted or newly registered domains
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from checkout pages to domains unrelated to the merchant or payment processor
Use of image beacons or encoded GET requests to exfiltrate data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor e-commerce sites for unauthorized changes to JavaScript, especially scripts loaded on payment pages. Use content security policy (CSP) to restrict allowed script sources. Analyze network traffic from checkout pages for requests to unknown domains, and inspect for scripts that access payment fields and transmit data externally.
